title: Photo-labeling neurons in the Drosophila brain
protocol: Configure the imaging software using the live scan parameters outlined in the materials and equipment section.
Tune the laser to 925 nm.
Image the sample using the 60× objective lens, ensuring the cell body of the neuron of interest can be located based on the dim baseline fluorescence of PA-GFP.
Image the targeted neuron at the highest magnification possible.
Select the ROI function tab on the imaging software.
Create a small area of 1.0 μm by 1.0 μm on the center of the soma of the targeted neuron.
Set up the photo-labeling cycle in live scan mode.
Tune the laser to 710 nm.
Configure the imaging software using the parameters listed for photo-labeling individual neurons.
Perform a timed sequence acquisition of the region of interest defined in step 3b.
Set the number of repetitions in the sequence to 70.
Set the period — the resting time between each repetition — to 10 seconds.
Adjust the laser power for optimal photo-labeling, within the range of 11 to 22 mW.
Run the photo-labeling cycle.
Wait 15 minutes after the completion of the photo-labeling cycle to allow recovery.
Repeat the photo-labeling cycle once or twice depending on the results.
Ensure a 15-minute recovery period between cycles.
Tune the laser to 925 nm for imaging.
Configure the imaging software using parameters for live scan mode.
Acquire the image sequence encompassing the photo-labeled neuron.
Add 12 μL of 2% PFA solution in well 1A.
Transfer the brain sample from the imaging dish to well 1A.
Incubate for 45 minutes at room temperature (22°C–28°C).
Add 12 μL of PBST in wells 2A to 6A.
Wash the brain three times by transferring it between wells 2A, 3A, and 4A for 1 minute each wash.
Wash the brain twice by transferring it between wells 5A and 6A for 15 minutes each wash.
Add 12 μL of stocker blocker solution to well 7A.
Transfer the brain to well 7A after completing the last wash.
Incubate the brain for 30 min at room temperature (22°C–28°C).
Dilute the mouse anti-nc82 antibody in the stocker blocker solution at a ratio of 1:20 to prepare the primary antibody solution.
Store the primary antibody solution at 4°C until use on the same day.
Add 12 μL of the primary antibody solution to well 8A when step 12 is complete.
Transfer the brain to well 8A and incubate overnight (at least 24 h) at 4°C.
Remove any remaining solution from wells 2A to 5A using a vacuum line on day 2.
Refill these wells with 12 μL PBST.
Wash the brain for 1 min twice, transferring between wells 2A and 3A.
Wash the brain for 15 min twice, transferring between wells 4A and 5A.
Dilute the Alexa Fluor 633 goat-anti-mouse antibody in stocker blocker solution at a ratio of 1:500 to prepare the secondary antibody solution.
Store the secondary antibody solution at 4°C in the dark until use.
Add 12 μL of the secondary antibody solution to well 9A.
Incubate overnight at 4°C in the dark.
Wash the sample by repeating previous wash steps.
Stack two reinforcement stickers on top of each other and place them in the center of a glass microscope slide.
Add a small drop of VECTASHIELD mounting medium to the center of the stack of reinforcement stickers.
Transfer the brain to the mounting medium and position it in the desired orientation.
Place a round, glass coverslip on top of the stack of reinforcement stickers.
Seal the edge of the coverslip to the slide with nail polish.
Keep the slide in the dark until the nail polish hardens.
Tune the laser to 925 nm.
Image the sample using a 60× objective lens.
Locate and visualize the brain area of interest.
Define a region of interest around or within the brain region of interest.
Take a z series of the brain region targeted for photo-labeling.
Select the PA mask function tab on the imaging software.
On each plane of the z series, define an area of the targeted brain region for photo-labeling.
Save the mask after defining the ROI in every plane of the z series.
In live scan mode, image the sample at the highest magnification to occupy most of the imaging window.
Acquire a series of scans spanning across the volume of the region of interest.
Define the area within the series of scans for photo-labeling using the PA Mask function.
Tune the laser to 710 nm.
Configure the imaging software using the parameters listed for photo-labeling groups of neurons.

Perform a timed sequence acquisition of the region of interest defined in step 25; set the number of repetitions in the sequence to 30 and the period — the resting time between each repetition — to 30 s.
Run the photo-labeling cycle.
Wait for 15 minutes after completing the photo-labeling cycle to allow sample recovery.
Repeat the photo-labeling cycle once or twice based on results.
Allow a 15-minute recovery period between each photo-labeling cycle.
Tune the laser to 925 nm for imaging.
Configure imaging software parameters for live scan mode.
Acquire image sequence of the entire brain volume encompassing the photo-labeled neurons.
